problem.text: Right triangle $ABC$ has leg lengths $AB=20$ and $BC=21$. Including $\overline{AB}$ and $\overline{BC}$, how many line segments with integer length can be drawn from vertex $B$ to a point on hypotenuse $\overline{AC}$?

steps.title: Where to start: slide the endpoint along the hypotenuse
steps.body: Picture a point $X$ moving along $\overline{AC}$ from $A$ to $C$, with the segment $BX$ attached to $B$. Its length changes smoothly, so the clue is to find where it is shortest and how it grows on each side of that point. First we need the hypotenuse.

steps.title: The shortest segment is the altitude
steps.body:
The shortest segment from $B$ to the line $AC$ is the altitude $BH$, which meets $AC$ at a right angle. Computing the area two ways, $\tfrac12\cdot 20\cdot 21=\tfrac12\cdot 29\cdot BH$, gives its length.
$$BH=\frac{20\cdot 21}{29}=\frac{420}{29}$$

your_turn.prompt: Between which two whole numbers does $\frac{420}{29}$ lie?

steps.title: Count the A side
steps.body: As $X$ slides from $A$ to $H$, $BX$ shrinks steadily from $20$ down to about $14.48$, taking each length in between exactly once. So each whole number in that range gives exactly one segment. Careful: the same length can appear again on the other side of $H$, and that is a different segment, so it must be counted again.

your_turn.prompt: How many integer lengths does $BX$ take while $X$ goes from $A$ to $H$, including $AB$ itself?

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: From $H$ to $C$, $BX$ grows steadily from about $14.48$ up to $21$, so it hits $15, 16, \ldots, 21$: that is $7$ segments, including $BC$. The altitude is not a whole number, so no segment is counted on both sides. The total is $6+7=13$. The answer is **(D)**.

wrong_choices.C: $12$ comes from counting the lengths $15$ through $20$ on both sides but forgetting that the $C$ side goes all the way up to $21$, which is $BC$ itself.
